$comment: SEC-106 / CTL-064 — the branch protection this repository INTENDS to have.
Read by scripts/check-required-checks.py. Two arms read this file and they
answer different questions:
--local   (pr-checks.yml, every PR) Does a workflow in this repo still
PRODUCE each context named below? A required check whose
producing job has been renamed is not enforced by anything —
GitHub keeps requiring the old name, which nothing ever reports,
and the PR simply waits or is admin-merged. That is this
ticket's title, and it needs no credentials to detect.
--live    (required-checks.yml, scheduled) Does the LIVE protection on
GitHub match what is written here? Scheduled rather than on PRs
because a pull request cannot change branch protection, so
running it in the PR gate would only add a third-party API to
the merge path (gotcha #23: the one control keyed on an external
feed is the one that froze the pipeline for eleven days).
⚠️ THIS FILE IS AN EXPECTATION, NOT A MEASUREMENT, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.
It was seeded on 2026-08-15 from what CLAUDE.md records under SEC-106 for
2026-07-30, because no branch-protection read was available to the session
that wrote it. SEC-106's own comment 15065 says exactly why that is not good
enough on its own: 'that is documentation, not measurement'. Seeding from the
documented intent is how the documentation stops being the only evidence —
the first --live run compares it against reality and reports any divergence
as drift. A red first run is therefore a SUCCESS of this control, not a bug
in this file: it means the sentence in CLAUDE.md was wrong, which is the
finding SEC-106 was raised to obtain.
Changing branch protection now requires a matching commit here. That is the
point (SEC-106 §6): protection becomes reviewable.
enforce_admins stays FALSE on every branch, deliberately. SEC-106 §2 'Do NOT
do these': promote-to-production.yml pushes directly to main with a PAT and
required checks have not run at push time, so enforcing admins deadlocks the
promote with nobody able to unblock it. It is recorded here so that turning
it on is a visible diff rather than a quiet dashboard click.
NOT COVERED HERE, stated rather than hidden: the `production` Environment's
required reviewer (SEC-106 §2, acceptance criterion 2). Environments are a
different API surface from branch protection and are Luisa's to configure;
asserting them is a follow-up, and until it exists nothing in this repo
proves that reviewer is present.

develop.note: Every feature PR lands here. CodeQL reported on all of them long before it could block one.

staging.note: Had no required checks at all until 2026-07-30 — the last stop before beta was the least-checked branch in the chain.

beta.note: beta.checklyra.com runs against the PRODUCTION Supabase project, so this is the last gate before real user data.

main.note: `guard` is main-chain-guard.yml's JOB ID — that job carries no `name:` field, so the context is the id itself. Rename the job and the requirement silently stops being satisfiable. That single rename is what this whole control exists to catch.
